finalSql:
SELECT c.customer_id AS cust_id,
       c.customer_name || ' <' || COALESCE(c.email, '') || '>' AS contact_label,
       COUNT(cl.claim_id) AS clm_cnt,
       COALESCE(SUM(cl.claim_amount), 0) AS tot_claimed,
       ROUND(AVG(COALESCE(cl.paid_amount, 0)), 2) AS avg_paid,
       ROUND(COUNT(CASE WHEN cl.claim_status = 'OP' THEN 1 END)::numeric
             / NULLIF(COUNT(cl.claim_id), 0), 4) AS open_ratio
FROM customers c
JOIN policies p ON p.customer_id = c.customer_id
LEFT JOIN claims cl ON cl.policy_id = p.policy_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name, c.email
ORDER BY c.customer_id

findings.title: || with a nullable column
findings.detail: c.email can be NULL. Oracle treats NULL as an empty string in ||; in PostgreSQL the whole result becomes NULL. Wrap it in COALESCE(…, '') or use CONCAT.

findings.title: Integer division
findings.detail: `COUNT(…) / NULLIF(…)` divides two integers. PostgreSQL truncates the result (1/3 is 0); Oracle's NUMBER division keeps the fraction. Cast one side to numeric.

proposal.explanation: The measured differences identify two PostgreSQL-versus-Oracle behaviors. PostgreSQL propagates NULL through ||, while Oracle treats NULL as an empty string, so the nullable email must be wrapped in COALESCE. PostgreSQL performs integer division when both COUNT expressions are integers, producing 0 for ratios such as 1/3; casting the numerator to numeric preserves the fractional Oracle result.
changes: Wrapped c.email in COALESCE(c.email, '') for Oracle-compatible concatenation.
Cast the open-claim COUNT to numeric before division to avoid PostgreSQL integer division.
Added explicit result aliases matching expectedColumns.
